issue.title: BigQueryValueCheckTrigger and BigQueryIntervalCheckTrigger fail while the BigQuery job is still running
issue.body:
### Under which category would you file this issue?

Providers

### Apache Airflow version

main (dev)

### What happened and how to reproduce it?

In deferrable mode, `BigQueryValueCheckOperator` and `BigQueryIntervalCheckOperator` fail with the message `Job running` while the BigQuery job is still executing normally.

`BigQueryAsyncHook.get_job_status()` returns the job state as-is for any job that isn't `DONE`, so a job in progress reports either `"pending"` or `"running"`:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/src/airflow/providers/google/cloud/hooks/bigquery.py#L2381-L2385

Both triggers treat only `"pending"` as "still in progress" and send every other status, including `"running"`, to the error branch:

`BigQueryValueCheckTrigger.run()`:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/src/airflow/providers/google/cloud/triggers/bigquery.py#L687-L695

`BigQueryIntervalCheckTrigger.run()`:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/src/airflow/providers/google/cloud/triggers/bigquery.py#L584-L590

Repro:

1. Use `BigQueryValueCheckOperator(..., deferrable=True)` (or `BigQueryIntervalCheckOperator`) with a query that takes longer than one `poll_interval`.
2. The job moves to `RUNNING`, and the trigger yields `{"status": "error", "message": "Job running"}`.
3. The task fails, even though the query would have succeeded.

There is a second problem in `BigQueryIntervalCheckTrigger`: the error event always uses the second job's message:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/src/airflow/providers/google/cloud/triggers/bigquery.py#L591-L595

When the first job fails and the second succeeds, the task fails with `Job completed` and the real error is lost.

The other triggers in the same file use `if success / elif error / else keep polling`, so they don't have this problem. For example, `BigQueryInsertJobTrigger.run()`:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/src/airflow/providers/google/cloud/triggers/bigquery.py#L187-L212

Existing tests only mock the `"pending"` status, never `"running"`, which is why this wasn't caught:

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/tests/unit/google/cloud/triggers/test_bigquery.py#L720-L724

https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/e92147c12aae3877b4842d7eb8de33233cb6d45a/providers/google/tests/unit/google/cloud/triggers/test_bigquery.py#L816-L820

### What you think should happen instead?

Any status that is neither `success` nor `error` (including `running`) should keep polling, matching the other triggers in the same module. `BigQueryIntervalCheckTrigger` should report the message of the job that actually failed.
